summary: ZnSe epilayers were grown on semi-insulating GaAs (100) substrates using metalorganic atomic layer epitaxy (MOALE) with dimethylzinc (DMZn) and hydrogen selenide (H2Se) as precursors at 350°C. The process involves alternating exposure of the substrate to DMZn and H2Se streams, followed by purging with hydrogen gas. The epilayer thickness was found to depend on the number of substrate rotation cycles. The photoluminescence spectra showed dominant excitonic emissions, indicating high purity and quality of the ZnSe epilayers.
evidence: ZnSe epilayers were grown on semi-insulating GaAs (100) substrates by metalorganic atomic layer epitaxy (MOALE) using dimethylzinc (DMZn) and hydrogen selenide (H2Se) source gases with a substrate temperature of 350°C. The epilayer thickness was examined for the different operating cycles and was found to depend only on the number of substrate rotation cycles. These results reflect that the growth of high purity ZnSe epilayers are achieved by MOALE.
